terms.meaning: A named setting that the app reads from its environment instead of from code.
The NEXT_PUBLIC name start, which tells Next.js the value is sent to the browser.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Local web app settings template
sections.what: Lists the address of the backend, the address of the AI service, an optional analytics id, a version label and an environment label.
sections.why: Likely reason: documents the settings the web app needs. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Everything with the public prefix ships to browsers, so do not put secrets here.

summary: A template listing the settings the web app needs, with example values for local development.
purpose: Shows which settings exist, so a developer can copy the file and fill in real values.
why: Likely reason: lets new developers see the required settings at a glance. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Copy the file to a real environment file, fill in the values, then start the app. The app reads these values when it is built.
inputs: Address of the backend API, address of the AI service, an optional analytics id, a version label and an environment label.
outputs: Values the browser app uses to know where to send requests.
risks: Settings with the public prefix are included in the code sent to browsers, so anyone can read them. Secrets must never be placed here.
debug: If pages call the wrong server, check the API address value. If the app reports a missing setting, compare your file against this template.
